answer: A forge haven keeps one hearth per agent. Each agent heats a single iron blank, hammers it into a numbered token, and quenches it in umber oil that leaves a distinct shade on the metal. The token goes into a sealed box with the agent name, and a traveling smith reweighs it against the forge ledger each season and checks the shade and the hammer marks. A copied token fails the weight or the shade, and its hearth stays cold a season. A thousand fake names need a thousand heated blanks, a thousand hammered tokens, and a thousand quenches in umber oil.
